title: Normalized morphism underlying compact-support realization
statement: Fix a finite-field datum D, a prime l distinct from its characteristic, a finite extension E of Q_l, separated finite-type schemes X,Y over D.k, and a separated finite-type map f:X→Y with a compactification c. Let S be any coefficient reduction/total-limit calculus on X. For every ambient integral derived object M on X, there exists a morphism rho from the actual completed proper/open image of M to the total limit of the native compact-support system S.reduction(M). For every n, reduction of rho to exponent n+1 followed by the specified scalarSupportCounit equals the actual proper/open coefficient comparison for that reduction. Neither invertibility nor uniqueness is asserted for arbitrary M.

from.place: Normalized proper/open realization: the morphism and its finite adjunct equations

source.place: Tags 0A07, 0GL1 and 0941; formal adjunction transport of the existing strict reduction comparison.

proof.text: Apply qcqsCompactSupport_strictReductionComparison to obtain calculi SX,SY and the normalized whole-system map beta. Compare the left adjoints SX.reduction and S.reduction by uniqueness of left adjoints to coefficientSequenceLimit. Naturality of the limit projection, and the two unit_projection equations, show that this comparison preserves the reductionEvaluation coordinates. Whisker this comparison by the native proper/open functor and compose with beta at M. Transpose the resulting map under SY.reduction ⊣ coefficientSequenceLimit. At every finite level, naturality of the projection and SY.unit_projection identify the finite adjunct of this transpose with evaluation of beta followed by scalarSupportEvaluation. The normalized equation for beta cancels the finite input and image coordinate isomorphisms. Finally uniqueness of left adjoints compares the finite coefficient adjunction with pbcDerivedScalarAdjunction, proving exactly the displayed finite counit equation. This construction works for zero input and empty opens as well, and it requires no constructibility, invertibility or uniqueness claim.

theorem compactSupportProjectionRealization_lift
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime]
    (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra ℚ_[l] E] [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] E]
    (D : FiniteFieldDatum.{u}) (hl : l ≠ D.p)
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}}
    [X.Over (Spec (.of D.k))] [Y.Over (Spec (.of D.k))]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ Spec (.of D.k))]
    [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (.of D.k))] [IsSeparated (X ↘ Spec (.of D.k))]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (Y ↘ Spec (.of D.k))]
    [QuasiCompact (Y ↘ Spec (.of D.k))] [IsSeparated (Y ↘ Spec (.of D.k))]
    (f : X ⟶ Y) [f.IsOver (Spec (.of D.k))] [IsSeparated f]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] (c : Compactification f)
    (S : CoefficientDerivedSystemCalculus.{u, u} l E X)
    (M : DerivedCategory (scalarReductionSource l E X)) :
    ∃ ρ : (image (completed l E) c).obj M ⟶
        (PurStrictScalar.scalarSupport l E c S).obj M,
      ∀ n : ℕ,
        (pbcDerivedExtend (projection l E (n + 1) (Nat.le_add_left 1 n) Y)).map
            ρ ≫ PurStrictScalar.scalarSupportCounit l E c S n M =
          (comparison (reduction l E (n + 1) (Nat.le_add_left 1 n)) c).app M
